notes: Bounded hypothetical positioning packets, not vendor assessments or evidence verification. Expected outcomes are human-authored calibration expectations. Repository tests check copy/wiring, case consistency and schema compatibility; no semantic evaluator is executed. The installed producer/verifier must independently replay them before activation. Apply identical expectations regardless of vendor, author, existing inclusion or owner association.

cases.positioning: A maintained installable agent runtime lets a customer schedule supplied agents, set tool permissions, retain session state and stop active runs. It bundles skills.
cases.reason: Customer-operated execution/state/authority is explicit; bundled skills do not change the runtime listing unit.
cases.policyClause: The offering runs agents for the customer and gives the customer meaningful control over agent execution, state or authority.

cases.positioning: A maintained marketing service explicitly offers only finished campaigns created by internal AI agents. Customers submit a brief and approve finished output; they cannot operate the agents, and no separate agent-facing capability or standard is offered.
cases.reason: Known finished-outcome-only shape without a qualifying agent/service boundary, not merely missing control information.
cases.policyClause: Finished AI business-outcome apps without a qualifying customer-operated agent or agent-service boundary.

cases.positioning: A shared AI marketing team lets customers approve, edit or skip its output. The overview does not establish whether customers control agent runs, state or authority, or merely finished results.
cases.reason: Output controls alone leave the decisive execution boundary unknown, not demonstrably absent.
cases.policyClause: If the positioning only describes approve/edit/skip outputs and leaves customer control over execution, state or authority unknown, hold for that fact
cases.clarification: Can customers direct or intervene in agent execution, state or authority, and through which control?

cases.positioning: A maintained agent tool catalogue combines upstream connectors with agent-specific capability discovery, task-scoped tool selection and normalized action errors so agents can find and invoke relevant tools. It does not own upstream infrastructure.
cases.reason: Named discovery/selection/error features specifically improve agent tool use; upstream ownership is unnecessary.
cases.policyClause: Using upstream services, producing structured instructions or combining connectors does not automatically disqualify it.

cases.positioning: A maintained browser annotation tool lets a human select a UI element and send DOM-linked, structured feedback to a coding agent so it can locate and fix the exact interface defect. The human operates the UI; the tool does not run the agent.
cases.reason: Structured feedback and element context are named features specifically supporting human-agent collaboration.
cases.policyClause: Maintained agent-focused libraries, catalogues, data services and human-operated feedback/context tools can qualify.

cases.positioning: A maintained open-source library provides coding agents with typed patch operations, conflict context and machine-readable patch failures. Builders install it into their own runtimes; it does not host or execute agents.
cases.reason: Maintained code with agent-specific patch behavior qualifies independently of runtime ownership.
cases.policyClause: Open-source code and libraries can qualify independently through Equip without being runtimes.

cases.positioning: A maintained data service combines upstream research feeds with agent-specific query plans, bounded structured responses and citation bundles so research agents can consume source-linked results within context limits.
cases.reason: Named response/query features serve a concrete agent research workflow; upstream data is not an exclusion.
cases.policyClause: Do not reject a maintained agent-focused tool solely because it is a connector, catalogue, library, feedback tool or data service.

cases.positioning: A maintained desktop context tool lets a person choose application history and send task-scoped context bundles with source references to their coding agent for continuing work across sessions.
cases.reason: Human-operated capture and task-scoped context features are specifically designed to improve agent continuity.
cases.policyClause: This includes tools and data access, discovery, memory, context capture, structured feedback, testing, permissions and human–agent collaboration.

cases.positioning: A maintained software tool compiles selected repository context and human annotations into structured, source-linked repair instructions for coding agents. Users install the tool and regenerate task-specific output.
cases.reason: Maintained workflow software generating instructions is distinct from a standalone prompt pack.
cases.policyClause: A maintained tool generating structured agent instructions is not thereby a prompt pack.

cases.positioning: An ordinary human-first CRM adds an MCP adapter to its existing API and calls itself built for agents. Its only agent-specific contribution is compatibility, a token vault, retries and a catalogue of 1,000 generic endpoints.
cases.reason: Known generic compatibility/repackaging; marketing, tool count and generic controls do not establish a purpose-built workflow.
cases.policyClause: Exclude generic products whose only agent-specific contribution is a compatibility interface, marketing label or repackaged API.

cases.positioning: A downloadable standalone bundle of agent prompt templates and skill files, with no maintained software offering or implementable interoperability contract.
cases.reason: Excluded standalone entry unit; shared file formatting does not make it a standard.
cases.policyClause: Standalone skills, prompt packs, templates and one-off snippets/scripts.

cases.positioning: A maintained named payment protocol explicitly defines agents as paying participants across independent clients and resource servers using a shared payment-required challenge and signed settlement contract. Conventional clients may use it too.
cases.reason: Agent role, resource payment need, cross-system boundary and shared contract are explicit; no runtime ownership required.
cases.policyClause: A shared, implementable contract is its contribution; running agents or managing resources is not required.

cases.positioning: A maintained named agent-to-application protocol defines shared streaming events for agent messages, tool activity, state updates and human interaction between agent backends and application frontends.
cases.reason: Concrete agent/application interaction across a frontend/backend boundary uses a defined common event contract.
cases.policyClause: Current first-party positioning must identify the agent role, concrete need and shared interaction or representation it defines.

cases.positioning: A maintained named agent-definition standard publishes a shared contract for portable agent identity, tools, permissions and entrypoints across runtimes. It is not an individual agent prompt, and only one implementation is currently described.
cases.reason: Portable agent representation is a qualifying contract; multiple implementations are not prerequisites for positioning fit.
cases.policyClause: Exclusive agent use, popularity, formal standards-body recognition and multiple existing independent implementations are not prerequisites.

cases.positioning: A general-purpose serialization standard supports ordinary software. Its sole agent relationship is that agents can also send the format; there is no agent-focused interaction or representation.
cases.reason: Incidental compatibility is not first-class agent design.
cases.policyClause: Generic HTTP, JSON and ordinary authentication standards do not qualify merely because agents use them.

cases.positioning: A generic image API accepts a named agent payment protocol and exposes MCP, but defines no shared agent contract and offers no other agent-specific workflow features.
cases.reason: Using another protocol is not Enable and compatibility alone supplies no independent Run/Equip fit.
cases.policyClause: Usage is not protocol authorship or a substitute for Run/Equip fit.

cases.positioning: A project with one brand describes a portable agent standard on one overview and a hosted harness on another. The proposed listing does not identify which unit it represents.
cases.reason: The standard and harness cannot silently share capabilities or a verdict.
cases.policyClause: When a standard and harness share branding or contradictory positioning, identify the exact unit or hold for clarification
cases.clarification: Is this listing the named standard or the hosted harness, and which overview describes that unit?

cases.positioning: Two permitted first-party overviews conflict: one describes customer-directed agent execution while the other explicitly says customers only receive finished results and cannot operate agents. No separate qualifying capability is established.
cases.reason: A material positioning contradiction cannot be rescued by repeated browsing or cherry-picking.
cases.policyClause: Meaningful contradictions in positioning produce a hold, not cherry-picking.
cases.clarification: Which current product mode is listed, and what customer execution control does that mode provide?

cases.positioning: The canonical page is inaccessible and the submitted overview gives only a product name and an AI label. No permitted alternative establishes an agent workflow.
cases.reason: Availability and missing positioning facts are not known negative capability findings.
cases.policyClause: An inaccessible page alone is not a negative fit finding.
cases.clarification: Provide an accessible introductory overview identifying the exact offering and concrete agent workflow/features.

cases.positioning: A product homepage is unavailable. Its permitted introductory repository overview describes a maintained agent memory library with task-scoped recall and source-linked context retrieval for agent sessions.
cases.reason: The permitted overview establishes positioning fit; homepage availability remains a separate recorded blocker, not capability verification.
cases.policyClause: If another permitted canonical overview establishes fit, record fit separately from the availability blocker

cases.positioning: A maintained API-only service provisions dedicated agent inboxes and agent-addressable message threads so agents can send, receive and continue email workflows. It also supports conventional software clients.
cases.reason: Named agent inbox/thread behavior supports a concrete workflow; API-only and nonexclusive use are irrelevant exclusions.
cases.policyClause: Human interfaces and operators are allowed; API-only delivery, upstream providers and nonexclusive agent use are not exclusions.

cases.positioning: A vendor offers both a finished-report app and a separately named programmable agent mode. This listing explicitly covers only the maintained agent mode, with customer-defined tools, schedules and stop controls.
cases.reason: The qualifying mode is the unit; the verdict does not qualify the vendor's unrelated app.
cases.policyClause: A vendor does not qualify every feature because one mode qualifies.

cases.positioning: The same agent inbox service adds an MCP interface to its existing REST API. Agent mailbox/thread behavior and the adoption boundary remain identical; a second listing is proposed only for the new transport.
cases.reason: The underlying service keeps the same fit, but the transport does not justify another listing; duplicate checking follows fit.
cases.policyClause: One product is not entitled to a listing per endpoint, skill, connector or transport.
